Infomaniak's investor page states '100% of staff and infrastructure in Switzerland' and its trust centre states 'The infrastructure is 100% controlled in Switzerland, with regional geographic redundancy'. sovereignty.closest_related_content: The general Terms and Conditions of Use (PDF, revision dated 24/04/2026) state at Article 22: '22.1 The Customer undertakes to comply with the Swiss and international laws in force during the entire life of the Contract. 22.2 Infomaniak will endeavour to respect the judgements of the competent authorities of the OECD member countries. 22.3 Any dispute relating to this contract ... shall be governed exclusively by Swiss law, the exclusive place of jurisdiction being Geneva, subject to recourse to the Federal Court in Lausanne.' That is a contractual governing-law clause, not a statement of the jurisdiction to which the ICT infrastructure is subject. The GDPR page contains the undertaking to 'Store your data in our data centers based exclusively in Switzerland, and never transfer your data outside our own infrastructure'. The sovereign cloud page describes 'A Swiss legal framework in line with European law, guaranteeing you compliance with the GDPR without depending on intermediaries subject to extraterritorial laws' and 'Strictly controlled access to data: No access to customer data is permitted unless explicitly requested, even for maintenance purposes, unless this is essential to prevent fraud or abuse'.

Infomaniak publishes substantial sovereignty argumentation, including a long editorial on the CLOUD Act, but it is directed at explaining why a Swiss provider is preferable rather than at making the two-limb disclosure. Note that Article 28 attaches to providers of data processing services offering services in the Union irrespective of place of establishment; whether it does so here is a legal question this dataset does not answer.

Second, limb (b): the measures sentence names three categories of measure but is framed as preventing 'unlawful access to or transfer of Customer Content', not specifically international governmental access to non-personal data held in the Union. Third, link rot: the hyperlink targets embedded in the addendum PDF are https://www.akamai.com/legal/compliance/privacy-trust-center/list-of-countries-with-server-points-of-presence, https://www.akamai.com/why-akamai/global-infrastructure, https://www.akamai.com/legal/compliance/privacy-trust-center and https://www.akamai.com/legal/compliance.
